item.title: The Indian Ocean Is Sounding the Alarm and Its Islands Are Among the First to Hear It
item.description: Across this vast ocean, the latest monitoring by Mercator Ocean International shows marine heatwave conditions ranging from moderate to severe. At the same time, the World Meteorological Organization expects a strong El Niño to intensify through August to October, with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole also likely to develop. item.title: Choosing the Next UN Secretary-General Cannot Be Left to a Powerful Few
item.description: As the 193 member states of the United Nations prepare for the opening of the 81st General Assembly session in New York City in September, the topic on everyone’s lips will be who to choose as the next UN secretary-general. This choice will be one of the most consequential decisions the international community makes this ... Read more

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Rising tensions in Gaza, West Bank
item.description: Amid illegal Israeli settlement surges, continued attacks in Gaza and the West Bank alongside tensions throughout Occupied Palestinian Territory, the Security Council is meeting at 10am (local time) on Wednesday to hear briefings on the latest developments. UN News app users can follow here.

item.title: More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal
item.description: Facing a projected shortage of more than six million health professionals by 2035, African countries are stepping up efforts to strengthen their workforce, with a new decade-long plan announced on Wednesday during a meeting of health ministers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

item.title: Deadly floods cause widespread destruction in China, Nepal
item.description: Severe flooding in China and Nepal caused widespread destruction and mounting death tolls, UN agencies reported on Wednesday as aid efforts deployed to help provide emergency assistance.

item.title: Land models sprout as degradation threatens billions of livelihoods
item.description: Promising efforts to restore degraded land are now in the spotlight at a time when 40 per cent of the world’s land currently faces degradation and drought, threatening the livelihoods of over three billion people, the head of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) said Wednesday, announcing three winners of its World Restoration Flagships awards.

item.title: Red Sea nations step up maritime cooperation as regional threats grow
item.description: From piracy and migrant smuggling to disruptions affecting global shipping routes, countries bordering one of the world’s busiest waterways are seeking closer cooperation to stay ahead of fast-evolving maritime threats.

item.title: Explainer: UN peace operations work to create, preserve peace
item.description: Supporting the first democratic elections after brutal civil wars in Mozambique and Cambodia. Disarming thousands of child soldiers in Sierra Leone. Helping to secure Namibia’s independence from South Africa. These are some of the contributions of UN operations around the world to help countries transition from conflict to lasting peace.
